newsitem.title: CANADA: TrizecHahn not in rush to dispose of Clark stake.
newsitem.headline: TrizecHahn not in rush to dispose of Clark stake.

text.p: TrizecHahn Corp is in no rush to dispose of its 46 percent stake in its Clark USA Inc refinery operator and would likely time its sale to market conditions, a company official said on Thursday.

"We're not in a situation where we need to get access to that capital immediately, so there isn't any urgency in terms of just trying to dispose of it for the sake of disposing of it," David Quan, TrizecHahn director of corporate communications, told Reuters.
"We're also trying to get as much value out of it as we can, so that's always going to be timed to what happens with the market," Quan added.
TrizecHahn's stake in St. Louis-based Clark was originally held by Horsham Corp, which merged with Trizec Corp Ltd last year to create TrizecHahn.

TrizecHahn has said it was looking to divest the Clark stake. The company said in its 1996 annual report the company "plans to divest, distribute or otherwise dispose of its 46 percent interest in Clark within a one-year time horizon with no loss on disposal anticipated."
"The bottom line is to try to get the capital out of the investment and redirect it toward real estate," said Quan.
Quan declined to comment on how TrizecHahn would dispose of its Clark stake and said the company was considering several options.

TrizecHahn earlier this year tapped debt and equity markets for capital. The company raised gross proceeds of US$150 million with an April share offering, and last month said it would sell C$300 million of debentures.
TrizecHahn closed down 0.10 to 29.85 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday on more than 470,000 shares.
